'''Food''' in Matcha Flavoured is eaten to heal and to gain [[effect]]s, not to fill a hunger bar. [[Hunger]] and [[natural regeneration]] are removed, so food is the player's main source of healing, and it replaces most [[brewing|potions]] as the source of status effects. The pack adds over 90 foods, most of them cooked or crafted from a small set of [[ingredient]]s whose hidden [[intrinsic]]s decide which effect a dish grants.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=Allowing foods to take over the niche once held by potions means that players will search for more diverse food intakes based on the potion effect they need. And because unlike potions, food stack, it makes obtaining potion effects far more accessible.}}</ref>

== Healing ==
[[File:Pumpkin Empanada.png|32px|left]]
Every food heals through a hidden {{EffectLink|Regeneration}} III effect that has no particles and no HUD icon. Regeneration III restores 1 health point every 12 ticks, so a food's healing is its duration divided by 12, rounded down: a [[Pumpkin Empanada|pumpkin empanada]] applies it for 96 ticks and heals {{Hp|8}}.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/crafting/pumpkin_empanada.json}}</ref> A few foods ([[Steamed Golden Carrots|steamed golden carrots]], [[Charred Meat|charred meat]], [[Charred Fish|charred fish]]) use Regeneration IV for 15 ticks instead, which heals {{Hp|2}}.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/kiln/charred_meat.json}}</ref>

The first line of a food's tooltip shows the healing as red hearts, one heart per 2 health points (a half heart for an odd point). The lines below it list the visible effects in the pack's tooltip style, for example {{G|Armor}} Resistance (8:00).

Because the healing is a status effect, it follows the vanilla rules for effects of the same level: eating a second food while the first one's healing is still running replaces the remaining healing only if the new duration is longer. Eating foods back to back therefore wastes part of the first one. The healing also stops if the player is already at full [[health]].

Most foods heal between {{Hp|2}} and {{Hp|12}}. The five [[#Oven meals|oven meals]] heal {{Hp|20}}, the most of any food.

== Effects ==
Foods give most of the effects that potions give in vanilla. The effect a food carries comes from its [[intrinsic]] ingredient: every dish made with [[pumpkin]] gives {{EffectLink|Resistance}}, every dish made with [[carrot]]s gives {{EffectLink|Night Vision}}, and so on. The more work goes into a dish, the longer the effect lasts. See [[Intrinsic]] for the full table.

Some foods have other effects:
* '''Cleanse maleffect''' ([[bread]], [[Honey Ginger Tea|honey ginger tea]], [[Ice Cream|ice cream]]): removes Poison, Mining Fatigue, Wither, Weakness, Bad Omen, Blindness, Darkness, Infested, Weaving, Nausea, Oozing and Slowness.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/oven/bread.json}}</ref>
* '''Cleanse''' ([[Milk Bottle|milk bottle]]): removes all effects, like a milk bucket.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/crafting/milk_bottle.json}}</ref>
* '''Aura''' ([[Glow Berry Mash|glow berry mash]], [[Glow Berry Jam|glow berry jam]], [[Glow Berry Crumble|glow berry crumble]]): makes nearby creatures glow. See [[Glow Berries]].
* '''Warping''' ([[Chorus Fruit|chorus fruit]]): teleports the player randomly, as in vanilla.
* '''Throwable''': [[Bubbling Mead|bubbling mead]], [[Pickled Toadstools|pickled toadstools]], [[Pickled Crimson Fungus|pickled crimson fungus]] and [[Pickled Warped Fungus|pickled warped fungus]] are splash potions instead of food, and apply their effect to everything they hit.

== Kinds of food ==
[[File:Canned Apples.png|32px|left]]
The developer groups the dishes of each ingredient into three steps:<ref>{{Cite video|quote=All ingredients with intrinsics have at least three corresponding foods. Simple preparation, preservation, and a meal.}}</ref>
; Simple preparation
: The ingredient cooked on its own in an [[oven]] or on [[kindling]], such as [[Baked Pumpkin|baked pumpkin]] or [[Steamed Carrots|steamed carrots]]. It heals {{Hp|2}} to {{Hp|4}} and "awakens" the intrinsic for a few seconds, which mostly hints at what the ingredient does.
; Preservation
: A jam, pickle, can or drink crafted from the cooked ingredient, [[sugar]] or a [[Mushroom|brown mushroom]] and a [[Glass Bottle|glass bottle]], such as [[Pumpkin Jam|pumpkin jam]]. The effect lasts a few minutes. Eating it gives the glass bottle back.
; Meal
: A crafted dish, usually with [[dough]], [[Estus Ash|estus ash]] and sugar, such as [[Pumpkin Empanada|pumpkin empanada]]. The effect usually lasts between 2 minutes 30 seconds and 20 minutes, and it heals more.

Beyond these, the pack has:
; Oven meals
: [[Green Curry|Green curry]], [[Japanese Curry|Japanese curry]], [[Paneer Makhani|paneer makhani]], [[Tonkotsu Ramen|tonkotsu ramen]] and [[Pumpkin Curry|pumpkin curry]]. Their [[stock]]s are crafted and then cooked for 15 seconds. They heal {{Hp|20}} and give an effect for 10 to 30 minutes.
; Plain foods
: Foods without an effect that are mostly healing: [[Baked Potato|baked potato]], [[cheese]], [[Chicken Nugget|chicken nuggets]], [[stroganoff]], [[gnocchi]], [[latke]], [[Fish and Chips|fish and chips]] and cooked meat.
; Secret foods
: Foods whose recipes never appear in the recipe book. See [[Secret recipes]].

Meat has no intrinsic. Cooked meat heals {{Hp|4}} and has no effect, which is meant to discourage mob farms.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=And since animal flesh holds no special properties, players will be less incentivized to manufacture slaughterhouses.}}</ref>

== Obtaining ==
Most food is cooked in an [[oven]], on [[kindling]] or [[Soul Kindling|soul kindling]], or crafted at a [[Crafting Table|crafting table]]. See [[Cooking]] for the stations, cooking times and how recipes are unlocked. Food also appears in chest loot, and the [[Cook]] villager sells a few secret dishes.

Several vanilla foods are replaced by the pack's versions when they're obtained:
* Apples dropped by leaves, carrots, tomatoes, glow berries, sweet berries, melon slices and chorus fruit from their crops, and food in chest loot, come from the pack's loot tables with its tooltips and healing.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/carrots.json}}</ref>
* A plain apple or sweet berries without a tooltip (for example from another mod or datapack) are swapped for the pack's version one at a time when they enter the inventory of a player outside Creative mode.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/remove_vanilla_items/apple.mcfunction}}</ref>

Vanilla recipes for mushroom stew, rabbit stew, beetroot soup, suspicious stew, pumpkin pie, cookies, cake, bread, golden apples, golden carrots, glistering melon slices and all vanilla cooking recipes for meat, fish, potatoes and kelp are removed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/pack.mcmeta}}</ref> Several of those items are reused as the pack's foods; see [[Renamed items]].

== Usage ==
=== Favorite food ===
{{Upcoming|type=section}}
{{Main|Favorite food}}
In an upcoming update, not in [[Matcha Flavoured 1.12.2|1.12.2-beta]], every employed [[villager]] that has traded at least once is given one extra trade: it buys 1 of a random food, chosen from 42 of the pack's dishes, for 1 [[obol]], once.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/favorite_food/trader_update.mcfunction|at=5bf7c3e22adaabf2416c83b709842cb9a053cb95}}</ref> The list covers most meals and all five oven meals.

=== Glass bottles and bowls ===
Foods eaten from a bottle (jams, pickles, cans, [[mead]], [[Melon Sorbet|melon sorbet]], [[Honey Ginger Tea|honey ginger tea]], [[Milk Bottle|milk bottle]]s) give back a [[Glass Bottle|glass bottle]]. [[Kontomire-Dandelion Stew]], [[bokguk]], [[Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal|apple cinnamon oatmeal]], [[Pad Thai]], [[stroganoff]], [[gnocchi]], [[Ice Cream|ice cream]] and the oven meals give back a [[bowl]]. Crafting a recipe that uses a [[Milk Bottle|milk bottle]], [[oil]] or a [[water bottle]] is meant to return the glass bottles: a hidden advancement gives the player 1 glass bottle per craft, or 2 for the green curry, paneer and pumpkin curry [[stock]]s.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/two_glass_bottles_from_crafting.json}}</ref> In 1.12.2-beta this works for those three stocks and for non-food recipes such as concrete and clay, but the advancement still names most food recipes by their old <code>main:</code> IDs, which no longer match. Crafting [[cheese]], [[dough]] from a water bottle, [[cake]], [[seitan]], [[Chicken Nugget|chicken nuggets]], [[gimmari]], [[Latke|latkes]], [[lumpia]], [[Buñuelo|buñuelos]], [[Fish and Chips|fish and chips]], [[Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal|apple cinnamon oatmeal]], [[Ice Cream|ice cream]], [[Glow Berry Crumble|glow berry crumble]], [[Chorus Mochi|chorus mochi]], [[pupusa]]s, [[Warped Stroganoff|warped stroganoff]] or curry and ramen stock therefore uses the bottle up. The other three [[stroganoff]] recipes aren't in the list at all.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/glass_bottle_from_crafting.json}}</ref> An upcoming update corrects every ID except cheese's.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/glass_bottle_from_crafting.json|at=5bf7c3e22adaabf2416c83b709842cb9a053cb95}}</ref> See [[Glass Bottle#Returned from crafting]] and [[Known bugs]].

== Advancements ==
{{See also|Advancements}}
* ''Powerful Flavors'': cook an intrinsic ingredient on kindling or in an oven.
* ''Now You're Cooking'': craft an oven.
* ''Pickles & Jam'': make any preserve. ''Doomsday Prepper'': make all 15 preserves (rewards 4 obols).
* ''Too Spicy!'', ''Hearty Curry'', ''Sweet and Spicy!'', ''The Best Soup!'' and ''Fortified Goodness'': make each oven meal (1 obol each).
* ''Hidden Flavors'' and ''Wait, you can make that?'': cook a secret ingredient and a secret meal. See [[Secret recipes]].

== Trivia ==
* The developer named ''Breath of the Wild'' as the inspiration for predictable ingredient effects.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=Breath of the Wild had something similar. I love that game. Being able to predict and anticipate the effects of certain ingredients I found really fun.}}</ref>
* Most of the pack's foods are custom-named [[Poisonous Potato|poisonous potatoes]] with their own model. Intermediates that shouldn't be edible, such as [[dough]] and [[flour]], are spawn eggs instead, because spawn eggs can't be eaten.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.7-alpha|quote=spawn eggs, even without entity data cannot be eaten}}</ref>
